metadata.title: Jensen Huang's return revives an old Wall Street trade: Bet on the comeback CEO

content.text:
Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia (NVDA) could be good for more than a one-day pop in its stock price.
Just look at the evidence from the case studies on the returns of founders like Apple's (AAPL) Steve Jobs, Starbucks' (SBUX) founder Howard Schultz, and Charles Schwab's (SCHW) founder Charles Schwab.
A new analysis of six high-profile CEO returns by Rand Group Research found that four of the six companies outperformed the S&P 500 over the three years after their leaders returned.
The biggest winner was Apple, where Steve Jobs' return in September 1997 was followed by a staggering 414% stock gain, versus 59% for the S&P 500 (^GSPC). The stock price gain reflected Jobs' innovation streak, which led to world-changing products like the iPhone and iPod.
Charles Schwab shares climbed 141% after its founder returned in 2004 after a year to rejuvenate the brokerage house, according to a New York Times account.
Starbucks gained 78% under Howard Schultz when he returned in January 2008, compared with a 10% decline for the benchmark. Schultz moved quickly to improve operations from a then floundering business.
Google's Larry Page delivered an 84% gain after returning in 2011, also beating the market.
There were exceptions, however.
Disney (DIS) shares rose just 14% after Bob Iger returned in 2022, badly trailing the S&P 500's 67% gain, while Under Armour (UA) has fallen 40% since Kevin Plank returned in 2024.
The takeaway for Nvidia investors? A founder's return can be a powerful catalyst, particularly when that founder has a deep understanding of the business and a track record of creating shareholder value.
But it's no guarantee. Jensen Huang has the opportunity to join a pretty impressive comeback club — but he'll still have to deliver.
Shares of Nvidia fell nearly 4% in premarket trading on Tuesday after a 31.2% surge on news that founder Huang had been reinstated as CEO. That came just 12 days after he resigned amid a personal scandal and federal chip-export probes.
"Jensen will be on a mission," EMJ Capital founder Eric Jackson said on Sozzi Unleashed.
Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the 'Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.
